title: Egoroff's theorem on ℝ^n with a closed good set and uniform convergence on its compact subsets (steps 5–6 of Simon's proof of Ch. 2, 1.5)
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and let C ⊆ ℝ^n = Euclid n be measurable, possibly with L^n(C) = ∞. Let η_k : ℝ^n → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) and g : ℝ^n → ℝ be measurable, and assume η_k(x) → g(x) as k → ∞ for every x ∈ C. Then for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is a closed set A ⊆ C with L^n(C ∖ A) < ε (L^n = volume) such that η_k → g uniformly on every compact Q ⊆ A (TendstoUniformlyOn η g atTop Q).
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Set (Euclid n)) (η : ℕ → Euclid n → ℝ) (g : Euclid n → ℝ), MeasurableSet C → (∀ k, Measurable (η k)) → Measurable g → (∀ x ∈ C, Tendsto (fun k => η k x) atTop (𝓝 (g x))) → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ A : Set (Euclid n), A ⊆ C ∧ IsClosed A ∧ volume (C \ A) < ε ∧ ∀ Q : Set (Euclid n), IsCompact Q → Q ⊆ A → TendstoUniformlyOn η g atTop Q
